profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CoreSite facility is in one of the company confirmed operating markets. Wikipedia coverage states that as of June 2022 CoreSite operated 27 data center facilities across 10 markets totaling over 4.6 million net rentable square feet, with key locations including Boston, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, New York City, Northern Virginia, San Francisco/San Jose, Santa Clara, Atlanta, Orlando, and Washington, D.C. In May 2007 the company acquired Chicago properties as part of a wider expansion. CoreSite began operating a Washington, D.C. facility in August 2005, one of its earliest East Coast sites after founding in 2001 as CRG West. CoreSite rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009, went public in September 2010, and was acquired by American Tower in December 2021. This specific market was confirmed as an active CoreSite location, but no market specific acquisition date or building history beyond the general company timeline was located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CoreSite CH2 occupies 168,000 square feet of technical space at 1432 S. Clinton St. in Chicago's West Loop. The operator has not published a megawatt figure for this campus, so no power-to-rack or power-to-accelerator translation is possible here. What the footprint does indicate is physical scale: 168,000 square feet of technical space is a large raised-floor envelope, though without a published IT load number the usable density and total compute capacity remain unknown. The campus sits 1.9 miles from 350 E. Cermak, Chicago's primary carrier-neutral exchange hotel, which is a proximity relevant to latency-sensitive workloads.

The six certifications on record qualify the campus to host specific regulated workload classes. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 address financial reporting controls and operational security controls respectively. PCI DSS qualifies it for cardholder data environments. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. ISO 27001 certifies a documented information security management system. NIST 800-53 signals alignment with federal security controls, which is relevant for government or government-adjacent tenants.

In Illinois context, this site has 44 mapped facilities in the state across all operators, and 6 of those have published megawatt figures totaling 236 MW. CH2 is not among the 6 with a published MW figure, so it does not contribute to that 236 MW total and cannot be ranked by power among Illinois peers. Its rank of 7 in the state context therefore reflects the site's position relative to published-MW facilities, meaning it falls outside the ranked set, not that it is the seventh largest by power. For an AI infrastructure decision, the absence of a published power figure is the single most relevant fact: until CoreSite publishes IT load capacity for CH2, the campus cannot be evaluated as a compute substrate on power grounds alone.
